papers.title: Editorial: Pests on the move: climate change and the shifting ecology of forest insects
papers.authors: Shulin He, Hengyu Yan, Amrita Chakraborty, Amit Roy
papers.source: OpenAlex / Frontiers in Forests and Global Change
papers.abstract: Climate change is reshaping forest ecosystems by altering temperature regimes, precipitation patterns, disturbance processes, and interactions between insects and their host trees. Among the most dynamic and consequential biological responses are the shifts in geographic range, seasonal phenology, voltinism, overwinter survival, and outbreak dynamics of forest insects (Pureswaran et al., 2018). These changes affect both native and non-native pests and pose increasing challenges to forest health, biodiversity, carbon storage, and timber production. Importantly, climate change interacts with drought, host physiological stress, disturbance history, landscape structure, and other environmental pressures to determine the severity and spatial extent of insect impacts (Anderegg et al., 2015;Simler-Williamson et al., 2019). To address these emerging challenges, this research topic, "Pests on the Move: Climate Change and the Shifting Ecology of Forest Insects", compiles seven pioneering articles, including original research, reviews, and perspectives, that bridge macro-scale ecological modeling, micro-scale chemical ecology, and landscape-level forest management. papers.title: Large-Scale Evaluation of Official Containment Measures Against Meloidogyne graminicola Golden & Birchfield in European Rice Fields
papers.authors: Mariangela Ciampitti, Anna Simonetto, Stefano Sacchi, Gianni Gilioli
papers.abstract: The root-knot nematode Meloidogyne graminicola is a major rice pest recently introduced into Europe. In Lombardy (northern Italy), an official containment programme has been implemented to limit its spread while allowing rice cultivation to continue in infested areas. This study provides a large-scale evaluation of the field performance of the phytosanitary measures implemented under commercial farming conditions between 2022 and 2025. Field performance differed among management measures and according to the phytosanitary status of fields at the beginning of each annual observation. Trap-cropping showed high operational performance while allowing continued rice production, and crop rotation was also associated with favourable outcomes. In contrast, prolonged post-harvest flooding showed more variable performance under local environmental and operational conditions. Analysis of three-year management programmes further indicated substantial differences among the management sequences implemented in the monitored fields. papers.title: Legume Fodder in the Age of Climate Change: Resilience, Risks, and Revolutionary Solutions
papers.authors: Muhammad Hayat, Rahime Cengiz, Muhammad Arif, Ferzat Turan
papers.abstract: Legume fodder crops are vital for sustainable agriculture and global food security because they fix nitrogen and enhance soil health. Legumes make up just 1.1% of the world's food supply, despite their many advantages. Cattle weight gain increases by 17% and milk output by 9.9% when forage legumes such as alfalfa and soybeans are integrated into livestock systems. But there is a serious threat from climate change. By 2050, yield decreases of 10-49% are predicted as a result of changes in precipitation and temperature. Elevated CO2 may promote growth, but it also causes a “dilution effect,” which lowers protein content by up to 30% and depletes vital micronutrients like iron (16%) and zinc (9.4%). A diversified approach is needed to reduce these dangers. Agronomic optimization, which involves modifying planting dates, densities, and water management, is one of the main interventions. ii) Soil and Pest Stewardship, which includes integrated pest management (IPM), reduced tillage, and cover crops. iii) Systemic innovation, which combines strong policy changes with genetic advancement through climate modeling. papers.title: Potential future economic impact of Vespula germanica (Fabricius) (Hymenoptera, Vespidae) in South Africa
papers.authors: David C. Cook, Simon McKirdy, Ruan Veldtman
papers.abstract: The potential economic effects of the introduced German wasp, Vespula germanica (Fabricius), on fruit and vegetable industries and households in South Africa were estimated over several decades if it continues to spread. The model described was used to simulate impacts on horticulture and wine grape production and household pest control services. The results suggest that, if unmanaged, the value of damage caused by this important pest could amount to US$160–300 million over the next 50 years. This implies that the investment ceiling for a prospective eradication program is approximately US$3–6 million per year. The results were highly sensitive to the rate of spread, indicating high potential returns on investments in spread-mitigation activities if eradication is not technically feasible.

papers.title: Economic benefits of aquatic invasive species management in freshwater systems: A contingent valuation study
papers.authors: Roshan Puri, Lucia Levers, Amit K. Pradhananga
papers.abstract: Aquatic invasive species (AIS) cause significant ecological and economic impacts, including habitat damage, degradation of water quality, and reduced recreational opportunities. While many of these effects are well documented, less is known about how the general public perceives and engages with AIS in regions with significant freshwater infestations. To this end, we conducted surveys of general residents and lake association members, a self-selected stakeholder sample drawn from a lake advocacy organization in Minnesota, USA, a state where over half of its waters (by area) are affected by AIS, with the objective of estimating households' willingness to pay (WTP) for managing AIS populations. Using a single-bounded trichotomous-choice question, we asked respondents whether they would support an annual increase in property tax or rent, with the generated revenue earmarked for AIS prevention, control, and containment. We conservatively estimate that general households are willing to pay $35-$40 per year, while lake association members are willing to pay $64-$75 per year. papers.title: Proposed Economic Threshold for Diceraeus melacanthus (Dallas) in Maize Under an Early Intercrop Cultivation System
papers.authors: W. P. Sutil, Letícia Carolina Chiampi Munhoz, Adeney de Freitas Bueno
papers.abstract: The Antecipe® system, in which maize is sown between soybean rows while soybean plants are still in the reproductive stage, reduces the production cycle of the soybean-maize crop system and, consequently, mitigate climatic risk for second-crop maize. However, the coexistence of both crops can intensify the 'green bridge,' favoring outbreaks of Diceraeus melacanthus. Thus, this study evaluated the host preference of D. melacanthus and the damage caused by different population densities to support management strategies in this system. The preference test was conducted in the greenhouse using cages (1.5 × 0.5 m) containing senescing soybean and maize at the VE stage, infested with ten adult D. melacanthus. Evaluations were carried out over three consecutive days at three times per day. The field experiment followed a completely randomized design with four stink bug densities (0, 1, 2, and 4 insects/m) in 6 × 4 m cages. When maize reached the VE stage, insects were introduced, and damage was assessed. papers.title: Artificial Intelligence Is Driving Cell Kinetics Studies in Cancer: A Narrative Review on the Evolution of Cancer Kinetics Studies
papers.authors: Tomas Koltai
papers.abstract: Quantitative descriptions of how tumors grow over time, from the interpretation of screening intervals to the design of chemotherapy schedules, underlie much of modern oncology. Tumor doubling time (TDT) is a fundamental kinetic descriptor of neoplastic growth, defined as the time required for a tumor to double in volume, mass, or cell number. As a deceptively simple metric, TDT occupies a pivotal place in oncology because it links microscopic cellular proliferation to macroscopic disease evolution, informs screening and surveillance strategies, and contributes to prognostic modeling. However, TDT is not a fixed biological constant; rather, it is an estimate shaped by tumor histology, microenvironmental constraints, vascular supply, immune surveillance, treatment exposure, and the assumptions embedded in mathematical growth models. In practice, most clinical applications rely on volume doubling time (VDT), particularly when serial imaging is available. Yet VDT estimates are sensitive to measurement interval, segmentation method, imaging modality, and whether growth is modeled as exponential, Gompertzian, logistic, or otherwise non-linear. papers.title: Prevention of Destructive Fishing in the Waters of Tual City: Effective Surveillance and Law Enforcement Strategies
papers.authors: Suharta ., Sigit Bintoro, Riyan Maulana, Ismi Isti Anah
papers.source: Crossref / International Journal of Multidisciplinary Research and Growth Evaluation
papers.abstract: <jats:p>Destructive fishing in the waters of Tual City remains a significant environmental and socio-economic issue, threatening marine biodiversity and the livelihoods of local fishermen. This study analyzes the problem using a SWOT approach, identifying strengths such as existing government regulations and rich marine resources, weaknesses including limited enforcement capacity and economic dependence on harmful fishing practices, opportunities such as growing global demand for sustainable seafood, and threats like illegal fishing and climate change. Based on the SWOT analysis, several policy recommendations are proposed, including strengthening law enforcement, promoting sustainable alternative livelihoods, enhancing education and awareness programs, expanding marine protected areas (MPAs), and creating market incentives for responsible fisheries. These strategies aim to transition Tual City towards sustainable fisheries management, balancing environmental conservation with economic development. Effective implementation of these policies will not only mitigate destructive fishing but also ensure long-term resilience for both the ecosystem and local fishing communities.</jats:p>

papers.title: Status and perspective of neonicotinoid insecticides from ecological toxicity and residue
papers.authors: K.S. Kim, Wasi Ullah, Hyo-Sub Lee, Jin‐Hyo Kim
papers.abstract: Abstract Neonicotinoids are a group of systemic insecticides that are used extensively in agriculture, accounting for approximately 25% of the global market. The efficacy and systemic action of these compounds make them effective agents that bind to insect nicotinic acetylcholine receptors (nAChRs). In particular, nitroguanidines had a dominant market share of approximately 86%, driven by insecticide activity in Asia and the Americas. However, the extensive utilization and contamination of these substances pose a significant threat to pollinators, aquatic invertebrates, birds, and mammals. These concerns have prompted significant regulatory actions, including the EU’s prohibition on the outdoor use of imidacloprid, clothianidin, and thiamethoxam; the extension of restrictions in France; and the phase-out of thiamethoxam and clothianidin in Canada, while their use persists at considerable levels in Asia and the Americas. In addition, synergistic toxicity is an emerging concern with Neonicotinoids and other pesticide groups. Therefore, robust monitoring of environmental media and development alternatives is required to effectively manage ecological safety. Such measures are necessary

papers.title: Taxonomic and ecological assessment of invasive plant diversity along an altitudinal gradient on Mount Gamalama, Ternate Island, Indonesia
papers.authors: S Suparman, D S Hefika, T Abdulrasyid, D K Aruni, K Surti
papers.abstract: This study provides the first comprehensive assessment of invasive flora along the Mount Gamalama hiking trail, Ternate Island, Indonesia, a volcanically active ecosystem of high conservation value. Through exploratory surveys and taxonomic verification, this study documented 31 invasive species from 16 families and 29 genera across an elevational gradient of 369–940 m. Asteraceae was the dominant family (32.3 %), reflecting its global role in invasion dynamics. Most species originated from the Americas (41.9 %), introduced mainly through horticultural and agricultural pathways. The community structure was predominantly herbaceous (74 %), with shrubs (13 %) and lianas (13 %), consistent with global invasion trends. Nineteen species exhibited reported allelopathic activity, suggesting that chemical interference drives colonisation and competitive dominance. Taxonomic ratio analysis (Family/species (F/S) = 0.516; genus/species (G/S) = 0.935) indicated a balanced yet evolutionarily diverse assemblage, with no species of conservation concern under IUCN criteria. papers.authors: , Eghbal Sekhavati, Reza Jalilzadeh Yengejeh,

papers.abstract: <jats:p>Background: Investigating human health during work importantly affect the safety and efficiency of the society. Different types of activity, including industrial, constructional, heavy duty ones, etc., affect the health of workers during their activities. In this study, the Multi-Objective Decision-Making (MODM) method was combined with fuzzy TOPSIS to investigate and optimize the air pollution risk affecting the health and safety of construction workers of Lar City, Fars Province, Iran. Methods: The comparison matrices (binary) and the Phillips–Perron test of different criteria and sub-criteria of health risk, including safety view, safety efficiency, understanding the risk, and risk investigation, were assessed to find the most influential factors for the optimization of the health risk of the workers. Results: Accordingly, the results indicated that “understanding the risk” followed by “safety efficiency” affected the health risk of the construction workers the most. However, among the sub-criteria, the most effective ones were “worker knowledge”, “manager knowledge”, “logistic specialized managers”, “modern facilities”, and “modern technology”. papers.source: Crossref / Journal of Advances in Environmental Health Research
papers.abstract: <jats:p>Background: Population growth, numerous factories, and many vehicles are the primary sources of environmental pollution and toxic elements in the industrial city of Arak, Iran. Methods: In June 2016, a total of 30 toxic element samples were taken from surface soils to examine their contents of lead (Pb), Zinc (Zn), Copper (Cu), Nickel (Ni), Arsenic (As), Chromium (Cr), and Cadmium (Cd). The samples were collected from 0 to 20 cm depth and measured using Atomic Absorption Spectroscopy (AAS) (PG990 Model). Results: The results showed that the mean concentrations of all toxic elements except arsenic had a higher value than the background values in the world. The Potential Ecological Risk (PER) index showed high and very high risk for the elements. For all elements, the Hazard Index (HI) values were higher for children than for adults. papers.title: Advancing Health Equity In Long Covid: Bioethical Considerations And System-Level Strategies For Post-Acute Care And Recovery
papers.authors: Qambar Abbas, Byunghun Jeong, Seung Won Lee
papers.source: OpenAlex / Scientific Electronic Library Online (Scientific Electronic Library Online)
papers.abstract: Abstract: Long COVID has emerged as a continuing public health challenge, with symptoms such as fatigue, cognitive slowing and shortness of breath affecting many people well after the initial SARS-CoV-2 infection. This review synthesizes evidence on prevalence, symptom, risk determinants, health utilization, and the wider social and economic effects of Long COVID, emphasizing prevention and health system preparedness. The analysis highlights differences across regions and population groups, rising pressure on rehabilitation services and notable consequences for employment, education and mental health. The study looks at fairness in resource distribution within overburdened health systems, equity in care access, and the protection of vulnerable groups in research and policy responses from an ethical standpoint. We underline the importance of harmonized diagnostic criteria, inclusive and representative research, and equitable access to chronic care services. We also set out priority policy actions to support earlier identification, team-based models of care and coordinated national strategies. papers.title: Generation of aphid-resistant wheat through plant-mediated RNA interference
papers.authors: Xue Zhong
papers.abstract: Aphids (Aphididae) are major agricultural pests that cause substantial economic losses through direct feeding damages and efficient transmission of plant viruses. Current control strategies heavily rely on chemical insecticides, which pose environmental risks and can lead to resistance, underscoring the urgent need for sustainable and targeted alternatives. In this study, we explored plant-mediated RNA interference (RNAi) as a sustainable strategy for aphid control by targeting two distinct genetic elements: the endosymbiotic bacterial gene Smrrl from Buchnera aphidicola, which is essential for aphid survival, nutrient provision, and stress tolerance, and SmDSR32, a novel aphid gene encoding a salivary peptide that is crucial for successful feeding. Initial in vitro double-stranded RNA (dsRNA) feeding assays confirmed that silencing these two genes significantly increased aphid mortality, demonstrating their importance as RNAi targets. Transgenic wheat lines expressing dsRNA targeting either Smrrl or SmDSR32 were generated. papers.title: Pest Risk Analysis (PRA) of Sitophilus granarius (L). (Coleoptera: Curculionidae) associated with wheat imports into South Sulawesi, Indonesia
papers.authors: Junaidi Junaidi, Ahdin Gassa, Baharuddin Patandjengi, Ervina Wijayanti, Shella Sawiti Guci
papers.source: OpenAlex / JURNAL HAMA DAN PENYAKIT TUMBUHAN TROPIKA
papers.abstract: The increasing demand for food, combined with advances in transportation and technology, has accelerated international trade and increased the risk of introducing plant pests and diseases from other countries, thereby threatening the sustainability of domestic agriculture. One important preventive measure is the implementation of Pest Risk Analysis (PRA). This study aimed to conduct a PRA by assessing the risk associated with Sitophilus granarius (L)., in wheat imported from Germany into South Sulawesi, Indonesia. A qualitative risk analysis approach was used. The results indicated that the likelihood of entry, establishment, and spread of S. granarius was categorized as moderate, while the potential economic impact was categorized as high. Based on the combined assessment, the overall risk was classified as moderate. The recommended phytosanitary measures for wheat imports into South Sulawesi include compliance with plant quarantine requirements and additional obligations. papers.title: Science and technology for food system transformation: Integrating edible biodiversity, grassland conservation, nutrition, and climate resilience in Ghana and Africa
papers.authors: Kwame Anokye, Huang Rong, Zhen-fen Zhang
papers.source: OpenAlex / Journal of Agriculture and Food Research
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Grassland ecosystems in Ghana and comparable African savanna regions support diverse plant resources that contribute to food security, ecosystem functioning, and climate adaptation. However, many edible plant species remain underutilized due to limited scientific characterization, weak integration into food systems, inadequate conservation attention, and insufficient application of emerging technologies for biodiversity assessment and management. This review evaluates the role of science and technology in supporting edible biodiversity conservation, nutritional utilization, grassland monitoring, and climate resilience within African grassland contexts. The review further examines processing technologies, nutritional composition, and food-safety considerations for underutilized edible species, linking conservation outcomes to food manufacturing applications and dietary relevance. A structured narrative review was conducted using records retrieved from Web of Science and Google Scholar, covering studies published from 2000 to 2026. papers.authors: Syed Arman Rabbani, Mohamed El-Tanani, Ismail I. Matalka, Shrestha Sharma, Manita saini
papers.abstract: Background Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is a leading global health threat requiring coordinated surveillance across human, animal, environmental, and genomic systems. Machine learning is increasingly applied to AMR data, yet its contribution to actionable surveillance intelligence, rather than prediction alone, remains poorly defined. Objective To map how machine-learning approaches generate AMR surveillance intelligence, to characterise their validation and implementation maturity, and to propose a framework distinguishing technical prediction from actionable surveillance intelligence. Methods We conducted a scoping review following JBI methodology and PRISMA-ScR reporting. PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched from January 2015 to May 2026 for studies applying machine learning or related methods to AMR surveillance intelligence. Two reviewers independently screened and charted records. papers.abstract: <jats:p>Background: Minimally invasive coronary artery bypass grafting (MICS CABG) via left anterior thoracotomy has emerged as a less invasive alternative to conventional open sternotomy (OPEN CABG), offering potential benefits in perioperative outcomes and complication rates. Objective. The aim of this study was to compare procedural characteristics, ventilation duration, drainage volumes, and postoperative complications between MICS CABG and OPEN CABG in a single-center cohort in Bosnia and Herzegovina. Methods. This retrospective cross-sectional study included 262 patients who underwent surgical revascularization between January 2019 and June 2023. Results. MICS CABG was associated with a shorter median procedure time (2.5 vs. 3.5 hours, p<0.001) and reduced mechanical ventilation duration (11.0 vs. 14.0 hours, p<0.001). Although ICU stay was similar (3.0 days, p=0.001), total hospitalization was shorter for MICS CABG (6.0 vs. 7.0 days, p<0.001). papers.abstract: The localization of prostate cancer by ultrasound remains limited by the lack of B-mode conspicuity and the confinement of clinically approved microbubbles (MBs) to the vasculature. To address tumor heterogeneity and ultrasound boundary ambiguity, regions of interest were defined from baseline B-mode images and segmented into the tumor core, rim, and a peritumoral area. papers.title: Divergent range dynamics among non-native Coleoptera: climate drivers and poleward expansion in multiple species
papers.authors: Stella M. Januario, Carmen P. Silva, Daniela N. López, Sergio A. Estay
papers.abstract: Introduction The expansion and contraction of species ranges result from population dynamics, species interactions, and environmental responses. As temperatures rise at high latitudes, some temperate species may be shifting poleward. As non-native species expand in range they threaten native biodiversity and disrupt ecosystem functioning, making range dynamics critical to understand for effective control programs. Methods This study examined the dynamics of the southern geographic limit of non-native Coleoptera species in Chile. Using occurrence data from 25 species recorded between 2007 to 2022, we evaluated how the southern range limit of each species responds to environmental variables, and whether the observed southward displacements are consistent with the regional climate trends. Results Model outputs provide significant evidence that the southern range limit dynamics of at least 11 species are linked to seasonal and annual fluctuations in temperature and precipitation. In addition, nine species already showed significant southward expansion, with displacements ranging from 200 to 1400 km between the minimum and maximum recorded southern limits. papers.title: Planting Power
papers.authors: Theresa Ventura
papers.abstract: This photo essay filters the Philippine copra industry through the lens of the cropscape, a mode of understanding the multiple assemblages and timescales by which rooted plants become mobile. One key story in this assemblage is Imelda Marcos's Tahang Pilipino – a model ‘Filpino home’ purportedly built exclusively out of coconut materials at the dawn of her husband's martial law regime and today popularly known as a ‘the Coconut Palace’. By approaching the Tahanang as a mid- to late-twentieth century iteration of a longer visual culture of coconut palm extraction, we see how Imelda Marcos’s imagined coconut future was deeply rooted in the extractive logics of a Euro-American colonialism that divided the globe into a temperate North and tropical South. The Tahanang Pilipino, I argue, modernised and nationalised a colonial history by naturalising the Philippines as a producer of tropical commodities for global consumption.

papers.authors: Isidora Silva‐Valderrama, Jane Theilmann, Melanie Walker, J. Boulé, Daniel T. O’Gorman
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Grapevine trunk diseases (GTDs) are one of the most important diseases in grapevines, threatening vineyard longevity and productivity worldwide. However, regional patterns of airborne inoculum remain poorly understood for many production areas, including the Okanagan Valley in British Columbia, Canada. Here, we developed and evaluated a droplet digital polymerase chain reaction assay for environmental assessment of Botryosphaeriaceae airborne inoculum. RESULTS: Across 2117 air-sampler extracts from 5 vineyards monitored over 4 years, Botryosphaeriaceae DNA was detected in 41.3% of the samples. At the regional scale, detection frequency and abundance was highest in spring (April-June) and again in summer (July-September). Abundance of inoculum and seasonal timing varied substantially among vineyards and years, indicating strong spatial and time heterogeneity in baseline inoculum pressure. Despite this variability, temperature emerged as a consistent predictor of inoculum presence and abundance. papers.abstract: <jats:p>Background: This study aimed to investigate the concentrations of heavy metals bound to airborne Particulate Matter (PM) in high-traffic districts of Tehran, Iran, and to determine the carcinogenic risk and Hazard Quotient (HQ) of these metals using a descriptive-applied method. Methods: Six indoor/outdoor stations were established in three high-traffic districts of Tehran. Each station was sampled with six replicates in winter 2018 (36 samples in total). After extracting the metals from fiberglass filters by acid digestion based on the ASTM (the American Society for Testing and Materials method), the concentrations of heavy metals were determined by an Inductively Coupled Plasma (ICP-OES) device. The human health risk was evaluated according to the US EPA (Environmental Protection Agency) standard method. The obtained data were analyzed by the Spearman correlation and Multivariate Analysis of Variance (MANOVA) in SPSS. papers.title: Aflatoxin contamination in dried fish: Sources, health impacts, Detection, Detoxification, and Control strategies in developing countries
papers.authors: R. Hiththatiyage, Ruvini Liyanage
papers.abstract: Aflatoxin contamination in dried fish is a growing food safety concern with significant implications for human and animal health. This review highlights the key factors contributing to aflatoxin contamination in dried fish, including its sources, influencing factors, health impacts, detection methods, and prevention and mitigation strategies. The contamination process is driven by interconnected pre-harvest and post-harvest factors, including the use of contaminated plant-based feed ingredients, inadequate drying and storage practices, high environmental humidity, and poor handling and processing conditions. These factors promote fungal proliferation and aflatoxin production throughout the production and supply chain. The review also highlights the toxicological impacts of aflatoxins, ranging from acute poisoning to long-term carcinogenic, immunosuppressive, and growth-inhibiting effects in humans and livestock, as well as bioaccumulation risks in fish tissues. Current detection approaches, including chromatographic and immunoassay-based techniques, are widely used but face limitations in sensitivity, cost, and field applicability. papers.title: Food safety and quality standards as trade enablers or barriers: insights from Tanzania in intra-African and European markets
papers.authors: Nicanor Obiero Odongo, Cecilia Moraa Onyango, Fiona Smith
papers.source: OpenAlex / Frontiers in Sustainable Food Systems
papers.abstract: Agricultural standards are increasingly vital for global trade, yet they present a complex paradox as both trade enablers and significant barriers for developing countries. This study examines the food safety and quality regulatory frameworks in Tanzania, focusing on the horticultural sector’s engagement with intra-African and European Union (EU) markets. Despite horticulture being Tanzania’s fastest-growing agricultural sub-sector, accessing export markets remains a challenge, with only 0.3% of the produce reaching international markets. Findings reveal critical gaps in national standards. For instance, while the Tanzania Bureau of Standards (TBS) has developed over 3,000 standards, those relating to fruits and vegetables often lack specific safety limits for different hazards. This regulatory void leaves domestic consumers vulnerable to food safety hazards while forcing exporters to adhere to costly private standards like GlobalGAP for EU market access. The results highlight a heavy reliance on traditional, reactive food inspections rather than more effective risk-based approaches, with inspection efforts disproportionately focused on export produce while neglecting local markets

papers.title: Status of beekeeping in Pakistan: apicultural significance, industry challenges, and opportunities for integrated genetic and disease research programs
papers.authors: Amir Said, Mah Noor Khan, Mohamed Alburaki, Shahid Karim, Abdul Majid Khan
papers.abstract: Beekeeping plays a vital role in food security, agricultural productivity, and ecosystem stability, contributing to honey production and crop pollination services. The sector in Pakistan represents an important but underutilized component of agricultural sustainability and the rural economy. Pakistan supports diverse apicultural landscapes shaped by different ecological regions, climatic variations, and floral resources, which influence colony distribution and management protocols. This review critically evaluates the current state of knowledge, traces its historical development, and assesses the contemporary status of beekeeping in the country, with particular emphasis on honey bee species diversity, the scale and distribution of beekeeping operations, and the socioeconomic contributions of the apicultural sector. In addition, it identifies major knowledge gaps and outstanding resea\rch questions related to honey bee biodiversity, population genetics, disease dynamics, climate resilience, pollination services, and sustainable management practices. papers.title: Pathogen-associated odor experience induces inherited olfactory avoidance in a parasitoid wasp
papers.authors: Shiyao Liu, Ge Jin, Jianghua Sun
papers.abstract: Abstract Odors allow animals to evaluate resources and risks, but the neural and inherited consequences of experience with ecologically meaningful odors remain poorly understood. Since both parasitoids and entomopathogenic fungi are widely used as agents in integrated biocontrol, we asked whether exposure to pathogen-associated volatiles can reassign odor value in a parasitoid wasp and whether the acquired bias is transmitted to descendants. Adult female Scleroderma guani were exposed, without host contact, to volatiles from Beauveria bassiana -infected hosts or to methyl cinnamate (MC), a representative component of the infected-host odor. Twelve-hour exposure shifted subsequent choices away from infected-host odor and MC, whereas shorter exposure produced different effects, indicating duration-dependent olfactory plasticity. The shift occurred without an explicit reward or punishment and is therefore consistent with non-associative learning. Unexposed F1 and F2 descendants of MC-exposed females expressed the same avoidance bias. papers.title: Does Soil Organic Matter Matter for Crop Productivity?
papers.authors: Fazal Sultanbawa
papers.abstract: Soil Organic Matter (SOM) is considered a vital component in soil-based agriculture. It is often used as an indicator of soil health and good soil management and is considered a prerequisite for sustainable plant productivity. However, these conclusions are not unequivocally borne out by evidence, especially from long-term field experiments such as the Magruder plots in Oklahoma, USA, where after more than 130 years of continuous wheat production without any fertilization, yields of 1 t/ha have been produced while soil organic matter declined from 4% to 1%. Furthermore, yields from soil-less production in advanced greenhouses have exceeded 600 t/ha/yr for tomato and up to 1000 t/ha/yr, compared to soil-based yields under 200 t/ha/yr. This is further evidence that soil and its various components are not prerequisites for high yields and maximal plant productivity. This narrative review will critically focus on the fate and role of SOM in crop production systems. The types of SOM, the effects of components such as humic materials, waxes, and organic amendments like composts, and the implications for soil health and the roles of soil microorganisms will be discussed. papers.abstract: <jats:p>Background: Today, soil pollution with heavy metals and petroleum compounds is one of the main environmental problems. This research was done to investigate the effect of drought stress, soil salinity, Piriformospora indica (P. indica), and MWCNs on biodegradation of diesel oil in the soil that contaminated with Pb and Cd under cultivation of triticale plant. Methods: Treatments consisted of applying MWCNs (2% [W/W]) in the Pb- and Cd-polluted soil that was simultaneously polluted with diesel oil (0, 5, and 10% [W/W]), and the plants used in this study were inoculated with P. indica. After 70 days, plants were harvested, and plant and soil Cd were measured using AAS (atomic absorption spectrometry). In addition, the degradation percentage of diesel oil in soil was determined. Results: Soil application of MWCNs at the rate of 2% (W/W) significantly increased the biodegradation of diesel oil in the soil in the drought and salinity (6 dS/m) stress by 11.3% and 15.6%, respectively. In addition, plant inoculation with P. indica significantly increased the biodegradation of diesel oil in the soil by 12.3%. papers.title: Shaping innovation : Studies of public funding for applied research in Sweden, 1970–2021.
papers.authors: Johanna Fink
papers.abstract: Innovation and technological progress have been identified as key drivers of long-term economic growth. However, not all innovation is supporting sustained economic growth or addressing societal concerns such as climate change. Against this backdrop, researchers advocate for active government intervention in shaping technological development, a role that governments have increasingly assumed in recent decades. Yet, it remains unclear where exactly public funds are channeled, and whether this is in line with wider policy objectives.This thesis offers empirical evidence on the allocation of public funding in Sweden between 1970–2021. To this end, a comprehensive database over public innovation funding is created, where individual public funding projects are directly linked to innovation outputs. The database has been used to investigate the quantitative dimension, direction, network additionality, and output additionality of public funding. papers.authors: Jessica Garcia-Lopez, Alyvia M. Martinez, Miles A. Newman, Adrian Sanchez, Abigail E. Cahill
papers.abstract: Zizania spp. (Mnomen [wild rice]) are annual aquatic plants found in rivers and lakes in Michigan, forming emergent beds that are home to many macroinvertebrates. Macroinvertebrates are key components of aquatic food webs and indicators of river quality. We compared macroinvertebrate community composition and diversity inside and outside of Mnomen beds in the Kalamazoo River (Michigan). Our study locations outside of Mnomen beds generally lacked any aquatic vegetation. We used leaf-pack collectors deployed in the river in 3 seasons. We identified animals collected using morphology and calculated taxon diversity and richness with Simpson's and Margalefs indices, respectively. Season and Mnomen presence both impacted community composition in our study area. When looking at macroinvertebrate diversity and richness, seasonal patterns were stronger than differences between habitat with and without Mnomen. Taxon richness was marginally higher, though not significantly so, in areas with Mnomen, but diversity was not related to Mnomen presence. papers.title: Sources, classification, analytical detection, and mitigation strategies for palm oil contaminants
papers.authors: Demas Aji, Supriyo Komaryantoko, Asranudin, Andreas, Heru Agung Saputra
papers.abstract: An overview of contaminant fingerprinting and traceability of crude palm oil products is introduced. The review focuses on process contaminants, mineral oil hydrocarbons, environmental contaminants, agricultural residues, and packaging/contact migrants. The formation mechanisms of 3-MCPD esters and GEs, with emphasis on the roles of chloride precursors, DAGs, FFAs, bleaching earth, deodorization temperature, residence time, and vacuum/steam conditions, are discussed. Analytical strategies are critically evaluated, including GC–MS, GC–MS/MS, LC–MS/MS, LC-GC-FID, GC×GC–MS, HPLC-FLD, ICP-MS, ICP-OES, AAS, and QuEChERS-based multi-residue methods, with emphasis on matrix effects, artefact formation, recovery, and method validation. The role of foodomics, chemical fingerprinting, lipidomics, metabolomics, spectroscopy, chemometrics, and DNA-based approaches in authenticating palm oil origin, detecting adulteration, and distinguishing crude, refined, recycled, blended, and contaminated oils is highlighted. papers.abstract: Fungal mycoparasitism is commonly viewed as a broadly conserved lifestyle relying on the secretion of cell wall-degrading enzymes and specialized metabolites. However, whether Trichoderma deploys a universal antagonistic program or dynamically adapts its molecular arsenal according to prey identity remains largely unknown. Here, we investigated the phenotypic and transcriptomic responses of four highly antagonistic Trichoderma atroviride strains confronted with damping-off pathogens from three phylogenetically distinct lineages: the ascomycete Alternaria brassicicola , the basidiomycete Rhizoctonia solani , and the oomycete Globisporangium ultimum . In vitro confrontation assays were performed between the four T. atroviride strains and nine pathogen strains (three strains per species). Despite notable intraspecific variation in pathogen sensitivity, all four T. atroviride strains remained highly effective against all tested pathogens. Comparative RNA-seq analyses during direct confrontation with one representative strain per pathogen species revealed strong prey-dependent transcriptional plasticity. papers.abstract: Wood processing industries generate staggering volumes of sawdust and residues. This research created a new way to turn wood waste into valuable resources, solving both environmental problems and agricultural challenges. Through step-by-step valorization pathways, sawdust was reused as a soil enhancer and processed into functional cellulose particles using chemical treatments-alkali digestion, peroxide bleaching, and acid hydrolysis. Characterization tests included: Zeta potential and size, Scanning electron microscope (SEM) and FT-IR. The zeta size showed nanocellulose populations at 95.82 nm and submicron cellulose (412.0 nm), with FT-IR spectroscopy proved they kept their natural structure by showing distinct hydroxyl (3339 cm⁻¹), hydrocarbon (2926 cm⁻¹), and glycosidic bond (1031 cm⁻¹) signatures. Scanning electron microscopy visualized the morphological transition from raw wood shavings to nano/micro-scale cellulose fibrils. This study used wood waste in four applications: water conservation, agriculture enhancement, bioremediation and medical wound healing.
